title: Hexapod rollout scheduler and guard rails
creator: Anya Patel
description: Implement a policy-driven rollout scheduler (codename: Hexapod) that composes traffic splits, multi-step schedules, cohort-aware probing, shadow traffic probes, and automated rollback guardrails. The engine should support declarative policies authored via a DSL and exposed in the Console UI for PMs/SREs. It must integrate with telemetry (latency/error budgets), SLO evaluators, and the routing layer so that traffic weights, step duration, and fail/fallback actions can be executed automatically or manually approved.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL that supports: weighted splits, step sequences, hold durations, warmup hints, cohort selectors, and rollback predicates
Console UI: create/edit a rollout policy and preview simulated traffic progression
Runtime: scheduler executes policies against live traffic with ability to pause/override via Console
Guardrails: automatic rollback triggers on configurable SLO breach definitions (latency P95, error rate, payload regression) with annotated reason
Shadow probes: ability to run 5-10% mirrored traffic to candidate variant for quality signals without affecting users
Integration tests and canary-simulator with deterministic replay to validate policy semantics
tasks: Design DSL grammar and examples (owner: Marco) - design doc linked
Console: rollout editor + preview flow (owner: Lina Gomez)
Runtime: scheduler core & controller (owner: Rajiv Singh)
Telemetry: expose aggregated windowed metrics and attach to policy predicates (owner: Priya Nair)
E2E tests: simulation harness and chaos tests (owner: Team QA)
Docs: PRD + user guide + admin runbook (owner: Product)
Security review and KMS considerations for private deployments (owner: Security)
Migration: convert two existing manual canaries to Hexapod policies (owner: Marco)
comments: 2026-02-11 - Anya Patel: Created ticket after scoping session with PM/Eng. Initial ask: support cohort-aware splits and shadowing. Blockers: DSL boundaries and Console surface area.

2026-02-17 - Marco Ruiz: Draft DSL prototyped. Decided to keep grammar minimal (weighted steps + predicates) and surface advanced features under 'expert mode'. Trade-off: reduced expressivity for easier validation and fewer UI states.

2026-02-24 - Rajiv Singh: Runtime prototype can apply weight changes with <100ms controller loop. Observed cache-warmup issue for KV-heavy models; added warmup_hint to DSL so scheduler can route synthetic probes to prefill KV cache before raising weight.

2026-03-02 - Priya Nair: Telemetry integration: added sliding-window evaluation (1m/5m/30m) and staleness guard. Suggested default rollback predicate: p95 latency > baseline * 1.4 OR error_rate > 0.5% over 5m with min requests threshold.

2026-03-05 - Lina Gomez: Console design review: added preview timeline and step annotations. UX feedback from PMs: make manual-approval steps first-class in the editor and show expected user impact when scheduling pauses.

2026-03-09 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented simulation mode and ran three historical replays from production traffic. Simulation revealed spurious rollbacks due to outlier events — we introduced a 'grace_period' setting to require consecutive breach windows before rollback triggers.

2026-03-12 - Security (Elena Park): Reviewed KMS/access considerations for private deployments. No additional crypto controls needed for policy definitions, but access controls must be RBAC-protected and audit-logged. Marked ticket for security follow-up (see dependencies).

2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Current status: core scheduler merged to staging (rl-runtime PR #8612). Console editor basic flows merged to staging (console PR #4279). Next: full e2e tests and GA rollout for internal teams for early feedback.
